title: Why Don't Submarines Get Crushed?
description:
Take an empty plastic bottle down to the bottom of a deep swimming pool, and it gets squeezed. Now imagine going three hundred metres under the sea. The water pushes on every square metre of a submarine with the weight of hundreds of tonnes. And yet, inside, the crew walks around in normal air, at normal pressure. Today, ten parts of a submarine, and why each one exists.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:09 1. The pressure hull
2:21 2. The depth limit
3:32 3. The ballast tanks
4:35 4. The trim tanks
5:43 5. The rubber tiles
6:49 6. The diving planes
7:58 7. The hidden propeller
9:03 8. The periscope
10:09 9. The escape hatch
11:16 10. The deep sphere
12:24 The verdict

Sources:
- Pressure hulls, frames, test depth and crush depth: Wikipedia, "Submarine hull" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine_hull and "Submarine depth ratings" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine_depth_ratings
- Komsomolets titanium hull and 1984 dive record: Wikipedia, "Soviet submarine K-278 Komsomolets" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_submarine_K-278_Komsomolets
- Ballast and trim tanks, neutral buoyancy: Wikipedia, "Ballast tank" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballast_tank and "Submarine" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine
- Anechoic tiles: Wikipedia, "Anechoic tile" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anechoic_tile
- Diving planes: Wikipedia, "Diving plane" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diving_plane
- Pump-jets: Wikipedia, "Pump-jet" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pump-jet
- Photonics masts on the Virginia class: Wikipedia, "Photonics mast" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photonics_mast
- Submarine escape and rescue: Wikipedia, "Submarine escape" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine_escape and "Deep-submergence rescue vehicle" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep-submergence_rescue_vehicle
- Bathyscaphe Trieste, Challenger Deep 1960: Wikipedia, "Trieste (bathyscaphe)" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trieste_(bathyscaphe)
